message.content:
**Your 7‑Day Paris Adventure – A Complete Itinerary**

> *Assumptions:*  
> • You’ll arrive on a weekday morning and depart on a weekday evening.  
> • You’re comfortable walking (most of Paris is pedestrian‑friendly).  
> • You’d like a mix of iconic landmarks, hidden gems, culinary delights, and a touch of local culture.  
> • Budget: mid‑range (≈ €120–150 per day excluding flights).

---

## Day 1 – Arrival & Settling In

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| **Morning** | Arrive at Charles de Gaulle or Orly. Take the RER B to **Châtelet‑Les Halles** (or the metro if you’re already in central Paris). Check into a boutique hotel or a well‑rated Airbnb in the Marais (e.g., Hotel Le Six, Hôtel Henriette). |
| **Afternoon** | Grab a croissant & café au lait at **Café Charlot**. Walk through the **Place des Vosges** and explore the art galleries. |
| **Evening** | Dinner at **Le Petit Cler** (French bistro). End the night with a leisurely stroll along the Seine, watching the city lights. |

**Tip:** Get a **Paris Pass** or a **Navigo Week Pass** (valid for 5 days) for unlimited metro/RER/bus rides.

---

## Day 2 – Classic Landmarks

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| **Morning** | Visit the **Eiffel Tower** early (skip the line with a skip‑the‑line ticket). Enjoy the view from the 2nd floor. |
| **Mid‑morning** | Walk to the **Champ de Mars** and relax with a picnic (pick up baguette, cheese, and wine from **La Grande Épicerie**). |
| **Afternoon** | Head to the **Louvre Museum**. Focus on the Mona Lisa, Venus de Milo, and the Egyptian Antiquities. Book a guided tour or use the audio guide. |
| **Evening** | Dine at **Le Comptoir du Relais** (bistro in Saint-Germain). Try the steak frites. |

**Optional:** Sunset cruise on the Seine (Bateaux Mouches) – book in advance.

---

## Day 3 – Montmartre & Artistic Vibes

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| **Morning** | Take metro Line 12 to **Abbesses**. Explore the bohemian streets, visit **Sacré‑Coeur** for panoramic views. |
| **Lunch** | Eat at **Le Consulat** (historic café). |
| **Afternoon** | Wander through the **Montmartre Museum** and the **Espace Dalí**. Stop by the **Place du Tertre** where artists sell their work. |
| **Evening** | Catch a cabaret show at **Moulin Rouge** or a more intimate performance at **Le Lapin Agile**. |

**Tip:** Wear comfortable shoes; Montmartre is hilly.

---

## Day 4 – Day Trip to Versailles

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| **Morning** | Take RER C from **Saint‑Marcel‑les‑Halles** to **Versailles Château**. Arrive early to avoid crowds. |
| **Mid‑morning** | Tour the palace, Hall of Mirrors, and the Royal Apartments. |
| **Lunch** | Picnic in the gardens (pick up supplies from **La Grande Épicerie**). |
| **Afternoon** | Explore the **Trianon Palaces** and the **Queen’s Hamlet**. |
| **Evening** | Return to Paris. Light dinner at **L’Avant‑Garde** (french cuisine). |

**Tip:** Buy a combined ticket for the palace, gardens, and Trianon. Consider a guided tour for deeper insights.

---

## Day 5 – Culture & Shopping

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| **Morning** | Visit the **Musée d’Orsay** (Impressionist masterpieces). |
| **Lunch** | Eat at **Café Campana** inside the museum. |
| **Afternoon** | Stroll down the **Champs‑Élysées**. Shop at flagship stores (Louis Vuitton, Cartier). |
| **Late Afternoon** | Climb the **Arc de Triomphe** for sunset views. |
| **Evening** | Dinner at **L’Avenue** (famous for celebrity sightings). |

**Optional:** Attend a jazz club in the Latin Quarter (e.g., **Le Caveau de la Huchette**).

---

## Day 6 – Hidden Gems & Relaxation

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| **Morning** | Explore the **Canal Saint‑Martin** area. Coffee at **Café Kitsuné**. |
| **Mid‑morning** | Visit the **Musée Rodin** (beautiful gardens). |
| **Lunch** | Try **Le Relais de l’Entrecôte** for steak without a menu (they serve only steak and fries). |
| **Afternoon** | Relax in the **Luxembourg Gardens**. Rent a small boat on the pond. |
| **Evening** | Sunset at the **Pont Alexandre III**. Dinner at **Le Jules Verne** (Michelin‑starred restaurant inside the Eiffel Tower). |

**Tip:** Book Le Jules Verne in advance; it’s pricey but worth the experience.

---

## Day 7 – Departure & Last‑Minute Souvenirs

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| **Morning** | Quick breakfast at **Du Pain et des Idées** (world‑famous pastries). |
| **Mid‑morning** | Visit the **Marché aux Puces de Saint‑Ouen** (flea market) for vintage finds. |
| **Lunch** | Grab a sandwich from **Boulangerie Poilâne**. |
| **Afternoon** | Head back to your hotel, collect luggage, and make your way to the airport via RER B or taxi. |

---

## Practical Tips

| Category | Recommendation |
|----------|----------------|
| **Transport** | Metro & RER are efficient. Use a **Navigo Week Pass** (€22.80) for unlimited travel. |
| **Dining** | Reserve tables at popular restaurants 2–3 days ahead. |
| **Language** | Learn basic French phrases; locals appreciate the effort. |
| **Safety** | Keep an eye on your belongings in crowded areas. |
| **Weather** | Pack layers; Paris weather can be unpredictable. |
| **Currency** | €1 = 1 Euro. Credit cards are widely accepted. |

---

## Suggested Packing List

- Comfortable walking shoes
- Light jacket / sweater
- Umbrella or raincoat
- Reusable water bottle
- Portable phone charger
- Small day bag for souvenirs

---

Enjoy your Paris adventure! If you have specific interests (e.g., art, food, nightlife), let me know and I can tailor the itinerary further. Bon voyage!
